principle: Canonical body architecture IDs describe measurable assembly geometry. Source terms such as bigfig, midfig, XL and muscle body are aliases/observations only.

architecture_families.description: Standard minifigure assembly and compatible leg variants.
Standard minifigure semantic assembly with elongated arms/legs, e.g. Woody.
Standard head/lower-body ecosystem combined with oversized torso and specialized arms, e.g. NEXO KNIGHTS Axl.
Broad/giant integrated body using standard minifigure head ecosystem, e.g. Hagrid.
Classic Hulk-style giant body with integrated head/body/lower shell and separate giant arms/hands.
Later giant architecture with separate giant head and optional hair/headgear plus giant arms/hands.
Character/creature-specific giant architecture; child architecture required when joint graph differs.
Third-party bigfig marketed as compatible with classic giant architecture; physical compatibility must be observed.
Broad/muscular custom torso/arm architecture retaining standard or near-standard head/lower body semantics.
Custom medium-scale body between standard and giant, often 3D printed and modular.
Approx. 7 cm Alpha Toys AF-family muscular body with visibly segmented/articulated arms; exact joints require physical validation.
Body built from standard construction elements to occupy a middle scale rather than a dedicated molded body.
Known custom body whose mechanical architecture has not yet been resolved.
